paragraphs.text: I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beseech you to walk worthily of the calling wherewith ye were called,
paragraphs.original: Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς ἐγὼ ὁ δέσμιος ἐν κυρίῳ ἀξίως περιπατῆσαι τῆς κλήσεως ἧς ἐκλήθητε,
paragraphs.translit: Parakalō oun hymas egō ho desmios en kyriō axiōs peripatēsai tēs klēseōs hēs eklēthēte,

paragraphs.text: with all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love;
paragraphs.original: μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης καὶ πραΰτητος, μετὰ μακροθυμίας, ἀνεχόμενοι ἀλλήλων ἐν ἀγάπῃ,
paragraphs.translit: meta pasēs tapeinophrosynēs kai prautētos, meta makrothymias, anechomenoi allēlōn en agapē,

paragraphs.text: giving diligence to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
paragraphs.original: σπουδάζοντες τηρεῖν τὴν ἑνότητα τοῦ πνεύματος ἐν τῷ συνδέσμῳ τῆς εἰρήνης·
paragraphs.translit: spoudazontes tērein tēn henotēta tou pneumatos en tō syndesmō tēs eirēnēs·

paragraphs.text: [There is] one body, and one Spirit, even as also ye were called in one hope of your calling;
paragraphs.original: ἓν σῶμα καὶ ἓν πνεῦμα, καθὼς καὶ ἐκλήθητε ἐν μιᾷ ἐλπίδι τῆς κλήσεως ὑμῶν·
paragraphs.translit: hen sōma kai hen pneuma, kathōs kai eklēthēte en mia elpidi tēs klēseōs hymōn·

paragraphs.text: one Lord, one faith, one baptism,
paragraphs.original: εἷς κύριος, μία πίστις, ἓν βάπτισμα·
paragraphs.translit: heis kyrios, mia pistis, hen baptisma·

paragraphs.text: one God and Father of all, who is over all, and through all, and in all.
paragraphs.original: εἷς θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ πάντων, ὁ ἐπὶ πάντων καὶ διὰ πάντων καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: heis theos kai patēr pantōn, ho epi pantōn kai dia pantōn kai en pasin.

paragraphs.text: But unto each one of us was the grace given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
paragraphs.original: Ἑνὶ δὲ ἑκάστῳ ἡμῶν ἐδόθη ἡ χάρις κατὰ τὸ μέτρον τῆς δωρεᾶς τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Heni de hekastō hēmōn edothē hē charis kata to metron tēs dōreas tou Christou.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore he saith, When he ascended on high, he led captivity captive, And gave gifts unto men.
paragraphs.original: διὸ λέγει· Ἀναβὰς εἰς ὕψος ᾐχμαλώτευσεν αἰχμαλωσίαν, ἔδωκεν δόματα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
paragraphs.translit: dio legei· Anabas eis hypsos ēchmalōteusen aichmalōsian, edōken domata tois anthrōpois.

paragraphs.text: (Now this, He ascended, what is it but that he also descended into the lower parts of the earth?
paragraphs.original: τὸ δὲ Ἀνέβη τί ἐστιν εἰ μὴ ὅτι καὶ κατέβη εἰς τὰ κατώτερα μέρη τῆς γῆς;
paragraphs.translit: to de Anebē ti estin ei mē hoti kai katebē eis ta katōtera merē tēs gēs;

paragraphs.text: He that descended is the same also that ascended far above all the heavens, that he might fill all things.)
paragraphs.original: ὁ καταβὰς αὐτός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ ἀναβὰς ὑπεράνω πάντων τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἵνα πληρώσῃ τὰ πάντα.
paragraphs.translit: ho katabas autos estin kai ho anabas hyperanō pantōn tōn ouranōn, hina plērōsē ta panta.

paragraphs.text: And he gave some [to be] apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers;
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτὸς ἔδωκεν τοὺς μὲν ἀποστόλους, τοὺς δὲ προφήτας, τοὺς δὲ εὐαγγελιστάς, τοὺς δὲ ποιμένας καὶ διδασκάλους,
paragraphs.translit: kai autos edōken tous men apostolous, tous de prophētas, tous de euangelistas, tous de poimenas kai didaskalous,

paragraphs.text: for the perfecting of the saints, unto the work of ministering, unto the building up of the body of Christ:
paragraphs.original: πρὸς τὸν καταρτισμὸν τῶν ἁγίων εἰς ἔργον διακονίας, εἰς οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: pros ton katartismon tōn hagiōn eis ergon diakonias, eis oikodomēn tou sōmatos tou Christou,

paragraphs.text: till we all attain unto the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a fullgrown man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ:
paragraphs.original: μέχρι καταντήσωμεν οἱ πάντες εἰς τὴν ἑνότητα τῆς πίστεως καὶ τῆς ἐπιγνώσεως τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰς ἄνδρα τέλειον, εἰς μέτρον ἡλικίας τοῦ πληρώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: mechri katantēsōmen hoi pantes eis tēn henotēta tēs pisteōs kai tēs epignōseōs tou hyiou tou theou, eis andra teleion, eis metron hēlikias tou plērōmatos tou Christou,

paragraphs.text: that we may be no longer children, tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, in craftiness, after the wiles of error;
paragraphs.original: ἵνα μηκέτι ὦμεν νήπιοι, κλυδωνιζόμενοι καὶ περιφερόμενοι παντὶ ἀνέμῳ τῆς διδασκαλίας ἐν τῇ κυβείᾳ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐν πανουργίᾳ πρὸς τὴν μεθοδείαν τῆς πλάνης,
paragraphs.translit: hina mēketi ōmen nēpioi, klydōnizomenoi kai peripheromenoi panti anemō tēs didaskalias en tē kybeia tōn anthrōpōn en panourgia pros tēn methodeian tēs planēs,

paragraphs.text: but speaking truth in love, we may grow up in all things into him, who is the head, [even] Christ;
paragraphs.original: ἀληθεύοντες δὲ ἐν ἀγάπῃ αὐξήσωμεν εἰς αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα, ὅς ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλή, Χριστός,
paragraphs.translit: alētheuontes de en agapē auxēsōmen eis auton ta panta, hos estin hē kephalē, Christos,

paragraphs.text: from whom all the body fitly framed and knit together through that which every joint supplieth, according to the working in [due] measure of each several part, maketh the increase of the body unto the building up of itself in love.
paragraphs.original: ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα συναρμολογούμενον καὶ συμβιβαζόμενον διὰ πάσης ἁφῆς τῆς ἐπιχορηγίας κατʼ ἐνέργειαν ἐν μέτρῳ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου μέρους τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ σώματος ποιεῖται εἰς οἰκοδομὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ.
paragraphs.translit: ex hou pan to sōma synarmologoumenon kai symbibazomenon dia pasēs haphēs tēs epichorēgias katʼ energeian en metrō henos hekastou merous tēn auxēsin tou sōmatos poieitai eis oikodomēn heautou en agapē.

paragraphs.text: This I say therefore, and testify in the Lord, that ye no longer walk as the Gentiles also walk, in the vanity of their mind,
paragraphs.original: Τοῦτο οὖν λέγω καὶ μαρτύρομαι ἐν κυρίῳ, μηκέτι ὑμᾶς περιπατεῖν καθὼς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη περιπατεῖ ἐν ματαιότητι τοῦ νοὸς αὐτῶν,
paragraphs.translit: Touto oun legō kai martyromai en kyriō, mēketi hymas peripatein kathōs kai ta ethnē peripatei en mataiotēti tou noos autōn,

paragraphs.text: being darkened in their understanding, alienated from the life of God, because of the ignorance that is in them, because of the hardening of their heart;
paragraphs.original: ἐσκοτωμένοι τῇ διανοίᾳ ὄντες, ἀπηλλοτριωμένοι τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ θεοῦ, διὰ τὴν ἄγνοιαν τὴν οὖσαν ἐν αὐτοῖς, διὰ τὴν πώρωσιν τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν,
paragraphs.translit: eskotōmenoi tē dianoia ontes, apēllotriōmenoi tēs zōēs tou theou, dia tēn agnoian tēn ousan en autois, dia tēn pōrōsin tēs kardias autōn,

paragraphs.text: who being past feeling gave themselves up to lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness.
paragraphs.original: οἵτινες ἀπηλγηκότες ἑαυτοὺς παρέδωκαν τῇ ἀσελγείᾳ εἰς ἐργασίαν ἀκαθαρσίας πάσης ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: hoitines apēlgēkotes heautous paredōkan tē aselgeia eis ergasian akatharsias pasēs en pleonexia.

paragraphs.text: But ye did not so learn Christ;
paragraphs.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐχ οὕτως ἐμάθετε τὸν Χριστόν,
paragraphs.translit: hymeis de ouch houtōs emathete ton Christon,

paragraphs.text: if so be that ye heard him, and were taught in him, even as truth is in Jesus:
paragraphs.original: εἴ γε αὐτὸν ἠκούσατε καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐδιδάχθητε, καθώς ἐστιν ἀλήθεια ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: ei ge auton ēkousate kai en autō edidachthēte, kathōs estin alētheia en tō Iēsou,

paragraphs.text: that ye put away, as concerning your former manner of life, the old man, that waxeth corrupt after the lusts of deceit;
paragraphs.original: ἀποθέσθαι ὑμᾶς κατὰ τὴν προτέραν ἀναστροφὴν τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν φθειρόμενον κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀπάτης,
paragraphs.translit: apothesthai hymas kata tēn proteran anastrophēn ton palaion anthrōpon ton phtheiromenon kata tas epithymias tēs apatēs,

paragraphs.text: and that ye be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
paragraphs.original: ἀνανεοῦσθαι δὲ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ νοὸς ὑμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: ananeousthai de tō pneumati tou noos hymōn,

paragraphs.text: and put on the new man, that after God hath been created in righteousness and holiness of truth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐνδύσασθαι τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν κατὰ θεὸν κτισθέντα ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ὁσιότητι τῆς ἀληθείας.
paragraphs.translit: kai endysasthai ton kainon anthrōpon ton kata theon ktisthenta en dikaiosynē kai hosiotēti tēs alētheias.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore, putting away falsehood, speak ye truth each one with his neighbor: for we are members one of another.
paragraphs.original: Διὸ ἀποθέμενοι τὸ ψεῦδος λαλεῖτε ἀλήθειαν ἕκαστος μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐσμὲν ἀλλήλων μέλη.
paragraphs.translit: Dio apothemenoi to pseudos laleite alētheian hekastos meta tou plēsion autou, hoti esmen allēlōn melē.

paragraphs.text: Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath:
paragraphs.original: ὀργίζεσθε καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε· ὁ ἥλιος μὴ ἐπιδυέτω ἐπὶ παροργισμῷ ὑμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: orgizesthe kai mē hamartanete· ho hēlios mē epidyetō epi parorgismō hymōn,

paragraphs.text: neither give place to the devil.
paragraphs.original: μηδὲ δίδοτε τόπον τῷ διαβόλῳ.
paragraphs.translit: mēde didote topon tō diabolō.

paragraphs.text: Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labor, working with his hands the thing that is good, that he may have whereof to give to him that hath need.
paragraphs.original: ὁ κλέπτων μηκέτι κλεπτέτω, μᾶλλον δὲ κοπιάτω ἐργαζόμενος ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσὶν τὸ ἀγαθόν, ἵνα ἔχῃ μεταδιδόναι τῷ χρείαν ἔχοντι.
paragraphs.translit: ho kleptōn mēketi kleptetō, mallon de kopiatō ergazomenos tais idiais chersin to agathon, hina echē metadidonai tō chreian echonti.

paragraphs.text: Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but such as is good for edifying as the need may be, that it may give grace to them that hear.
paragraphs.original: πᾶς λόγος σαπρὸς ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν μὴ ἐκπορευέσθω, ἀλλὰ εἴ τις ἀγαθὸς πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χρείας, ἵνα δῷ χάριν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: pas logos sapros ek tou stomatos hymōn mē ekporeuesthō, alla ei tis agathos pros oikodomēn tēs chreias, hina dō charin tois akouousin.

paragraphs.text: And grieve not the Holy Spirit of God, in whom ye were sealed unto the day of redemption.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μὴ λυπεῖτε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν ᾧ ἐσφραγίσθητε εἰς ἡμέραν ἀπολυτρώσεως.
paragraphs.translit: kai mē lypeite to pneuma to hagion tou theou, en hō esphragisthēte eis hēmeran apolytrōseōs.

paragraphs.text: Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamor, and railing, be put away from you, with all malice:
paragraphs.original: πᾶσα πικρία καὶ θυμὸς καὶ ὀργὴ καὶ κραυγὴ καὶ βλασφημία ἀρθήτω ἀφʼ ὑμῶν σὺν πάσῃ κακίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: pasa pikria kai thymos kai orgē kai kraugē kai blasphēmia arthētō aphʼ hymōn syn pasē kakia.

paragraphs.text: and be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving each other, even as God also in Christ forgave you.
paragraphs.original: γίνεσθε εἰς ἀλλήλους χρηστοί, εὔσπλαγχνοι, χαριζόμενοι ἑαυτοῖς καθὼς καὶ ὁ θεὸς ἐν Χριστῷ ἐχαρίσατο ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ginesthe eis allēlous chrēstoi, eusplanchnoi, charizomenoi heautois kathōs kai ho theos en Christō echarisato hymin.
